title: Latest order per customer
statementMd:
For each customer who ordered, show their name and the id and date of their most recent order.

Expected columns: `name`, `order_id`, `order_date`.

Tables: `customers`, `products`, `orders`, `order_items`.

Row order does not matter.
hints: `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC)`.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH ranked AS (SELECT o.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS rn FROM orders o) SELECT c.name, r.id AS order_id, r.order_date FROM ranked r JOIN customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id WHERE r.rn = 1;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
